title: Basement Suite Rental Income in Winnipeg: Rules, Rent and Payback
metaTitle: Basement Suite Rental Income in Winnipeg | Bridgeland
metaDescription: Renting out a Winnipeg basement suite: permits, code ceiling heights, egress and fire separation, CMHC rent figures, and a payback calculator.
excerpt: When a Winnipeg basement suite can legally be rented, the building code numbers that shape it, what CMHC’s rent survey shows, and a payback calculator that uses your own quote.
answer: You can rent out a Winnipeg basement suite once zoning allows it, it has development, building, electrical and plumbing permits, and it passes final inspection. CMHC’s rental survey doesn’t cover basement suites, but its October 2025 average for a one-bedroom Winnipeg apartment was $1,232 a month. Payback is your quoted build cost divided by a year of net rent.

faqs.q: How much rent can I charge for a basement suite in Winnipeg?
faqs.a: There’s no official average for basement suites. CMHC’s October 2025 survey put the average Winnipeg rent for a one-bedroom purpose-built apartment at $1,232 a month, and a bachelor at $915. A suite’s rent depends on its size, light, entrance and what’s included, so compare current listings for similar suites before you set yours.

faqs.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a basement suite?
faqs.a: At least 1.95 m (about 6 ft. 5 in.), with 1.85 m (about 6 ft. 1 in.) under beams and ducts, under the 2020 National Building Code as Manitoba adopted it. The City’s guide for ordinary basements uses 2.1 m, so ask the City’s plan examiners which figure applies to your drawings.

faqs.q: Does a basement suite need a fire separation from the main house?
faqs.a: It needs a separation, but not necessarily a fire-rated one. In a house with a secondary suite, the code accepts a smoke-tight barrier of at least 12.7 mm (½ in.) gypsum board on both sides of the walls between the units and under the floor framing. Doors in it are solid-core wood, at least 45 mm thick, with a self-closer.

faqs.q: Is there a government loan or grant for building a basement suite in Manitoba?
faqs.a: Not from the programs most sites mention. Budget 2025 says the Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program will not be implemented, and the Province’s Secondary Suites Program page said in August 2025 that applications weren’t being accepted. CMHC-insured refinancing of up to 90% of the home’s value, including the value the suite adds, is available through lenders, on CMHC’s conditions.

faqs.q: How long does a basement suite take to pay for itself?
faqs.a: It depends on your quote and your rent. Divide the build cost by a year of net rent, which is rent less vacancy and the costs you pay. At CMHC’s one-bedroom average and 2.8% vacancy, each $10,000 of build cost takes about eight months of rent to recover, before utilities, insurance, maintenance, financing and tax.

blocks.x: A basement suite can bring in rent every month, but only once it’s legal, and only if the numbers work for your house. That comes down to three things: whether the City allows a suite on your lot, what the building code asks of the space, and what a tenant will realistically pay.

This guide uses the City of Winnipeg’s secondary suite pages and forms, the 2020 National Building Code as Manitoba adopted it, and CMHC’s October 2025 rental survey, with the date we checked each one listed under Sources. It’s general information, not legal, tax or financial advice, and the City’s documents and staff govern for your property.
When can you legally rent out a basement suite in Winnipeg?

When zoning allows it, the permits are in place and the work has passed final inspection. The City says attached suites, such as a basement suite, may be permitted in every zoning district that allows single-family homes: A, RR5, RR2, R1, R2, RMF, RMU and C1. Only one suite, attached or detached, is allowed per lot.

Before construction, homeowners need a development permit and a building permit, and the City requires separate electrical and plumbing permits. Its housing inspections page says the final inspection confirms that all work under all permits is complete and the project is ready for occupancy or use. Plan a tenant’s move-in date after that inspection, not before.

If a suite doesn’t meet the Zoning By-law’s use-specific standards, the City’s April 2026 form says a conditional use application is required. The fee to establish an attached suite that way is $274 plus GST ($287.70), and the City estimates about 6 to 8 weeks of processing, plus 14 days of public notice.
Size limits, parking and the rules for garden and garage suites are covered in our guide to [secondary suite rules in Winnipeg](/blog/secondary-suite-rules-winnipeg).
Can you rent out a suite that was built without permits?

Get it approved first. If an existing attached suite doesn’t meet the use-specific standards, the City’s form calls for a conditional use application to maintain it. The fee is $660 plus GST ($693.00), and if the application is refused, the same conditional use can’t be applied for again for one year.

Permit Amnesty may not help here. The City’s program is for work at a homeowner’s primary residence, and its page lists rental properties as not eligible, so ask the City how that applies to a house with a rented suite. Our guide to [checking a home’s permit history](/blog/check-permit-history-winnipeg-house) shows how to find out what was permitted.
What ceiling height does a basement suite need?

At least 1.95 m (about 6 ft. 5 in.), with at least 1.85 m (about 6 ft. 1 in.) of clear height under beams and ducts. Those are the secondary suite minimums in the 2020 National Building Code, which Manitoba adopted with its own amendments on January 1, 2024.

Where the ceilings meet that minimum, doorways inside the suite can be sized for doors 1,890 mm (about 6 ft. 2 in.) high. The City’s guide for ordinary basement development uses 2.1 m (6 ft. 11 in.) for finished rooms, so ask its plan examiners which figure applies before you plan around a low ceiling.
What are the egress window rules for a suite bedroom?
Unless the suite is sprinklered, each bedroom needs an outside window or exterior door that opens from the inside without keys, tools or special knowledge. A bedroom window must:
give an unobstructed opening of at least 0.35 m² (3.77 sq. ft.), with no dimension under 380 mm (15 in.)
stay open on its own in an emergency, without extra support
have at least 760 mm (2 ft. 6 in.) of clear space in front of it where it opens into a window well

The City’s basement guide uses the same minimums for any basement bedroom. A new or enlarged opening in a foundation wall needs drawings stamped by an engineer, and our guide to [basement development permits](/blog/basement-development-permits-winnipeg) covers the rest of the City’s checklist.
What fire separation, alarms and sound control does a suite need?

A smoke-tight drywall barrier between the two units, smoke alarms interconnected across both, and a sound-rated separation. A house with a suite gets lighter rules than an apartment building; the table sets out the main requirements in Part 9 of the code, with the article numbers to show your designer or the City.

blocks.x: Plan the entrance with the exits. The City describes an attached suite as having a separate entrance, and each household must reach its own services, such as the panel, without passing through the other unit. The code lets the units in a house with a suite share an exit stair without the second, separate exit it would otherwise require.
What can a basement suite rent for in Winnipeg?

No one publishes an official basement-suite rent, so the closest benchmark is CMHC’s Rental Market Survey. Run every October, it covers privately initiated rental buildings with at least three units, so its figures show what Winnipeg tenants pay for an apartment, not for a suite.

blocks.x: Rents rose over the year, and so did vacancy. The average one-bedroom rent went from $1,179 in October 2024 to $1,232, and the overall vacancy rate from 1.7% to 2.8%. CMHC reports that conditions softened across the Winnipeg area in 2025, with vacancy rising in suburban neighbourhoods.

A suite’s own rent depends on its size, light, ceiling height, entrance and what’s included, such as utilities or parking. Compare current listings for similar suites near you, then use the figure you expect in the calculator below.
How do you work out a basement suite’s payback?

With your own numbers. Use the total from a written quote for the suite and a rent you’ve checked against local listings. We don’t publish suite prices, because each one depends on the basement it starts from. The calculator works out three figures:
**Gross yield**: a year of rent divided by the build cost.
**Net monthly income**: the rent, less vacancy and the monthly costs you’ll pay, such as utilities, insurance and maintenance.
**Simple payback**: the build cost divided by a year of net income.

As an example, take CMHC’s one-bedroom average of $1,232 a month and its 2.8% vacancy rate. That’s about $14,370 of rent a year, so each $10,000 of build cost takes about eight months of rent to recover, before any costs you pay.

Simple payback leaves out financing, interest, tax, rent increases and any change in your home’s value. It’s a planning estimate, not financial advice, so check the numbers with your lender and a tax professional before you commit.
How can you pay for a suite, and what help exists?

The main federal tool is insured refinancing. Since January 15, 2025, lenders can offer CMHC-insured refinancing to homeowners adding a secondary suite, on the terms in the table. The two suite loan programs many sites still mention aren’t available.

blocks.x: Rent from a suite is also reported for income tax. The Canada Revenue Agency says form T776, Statement of Real Estate Rentals, is used by rental property owners to report rental income and expenses. Ask a tax professional how a suite affects your return before you rely on a payback figure.

Building the suite for a family member instead? A federal tax credit may apply; see our guides to [Manitoba renovation tax credits and rebates](/blog/manitoba-renovation-tax-credits-rebates) and [home renovation financing in Canada](/blog/home-renovation-financing-canada).
When do you need a designer or engineer for a suite?

Most suites start on paper. The City’s basement permit form asks for a fully dimensioned floor plan showing each room’s use, every door and window, and the electrical and plumbing layout. Some parts of a suite need a professional:
An engineer’s stamp on drawings for any window added or enlarged in a foundation wall.
Engineered drawings for major structural work, such as changing beams or teleposts.
For a garden or garage suite, a water and sewer site servicing plan prepared by a Manitoba land surveyor or professional civil engineer.
The heating layout is worth settling early too. The code’s rules on separate ducts and controls decide where ducts run, and that affects the ceiling heights you can keep.
